title: Optimized Protocol for Chelex-based Extraction of DNA from Historical Skeletal Remains
author: Wera M Schmerer
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.pex-1652/v1
materials: 1300µl Chelex-100-solution (5% in sterile Water, e.g. Ampuwa ®, Fresenius or 18 Megohm Water, Sigma) and 500µl proteinase K-solution (20mg/ml, e.g. Qiagen) are added.

The mixture is vortexed briefly (5-10sec, Vortex Genie 2, VWRbrand) and incubated at 56˚C and constant shaking at 300rpm (Thermomixer, Eppendorf) for a duration appropriate for the DNA degradation expected in the material to be analyzed (cf. 2, 5 and Tab. 2).
The mix is vortexed again briefly (5-10sec) and incubated at 95˚C for 8min (Thermomixer, Eppendorf) to denature and deactivate the proteinase.

The mixture is left to cool down slowly to room temperature (Thermomixer, Eppendorf) and the aqueous portion is separated from the Chelex resin by centrifugation for 6min at 4000rpm (Centrifuge 5804, Eppendorf).
Precipitation is carried out for 30min at RT.

The DNA is eluted in 50µl sterile water (e.g. Ampuwa ®, Fresenius or 18 Megohm Water, Sigma) for 5min at 50˚C and constant shaking at 300rpm (Termomixer, Eppendorf) and the eluate transferred to a 2ml tube (Safelock, Eppendorf). To ensure optimal stability of the extracted DNA, storage of the extract with silica at -20˚C is recommended 36 .

steps.title: Prepare Bone Sample
steps.instruction: Obtain a 1x1cm (ca. 1g) sample from the mid shaft region of a long bone.

steps.title: Decontaminate Bone Surfaces
steps.instruction: Remove exposed surfaces of the bone sample using a sterile scalpel to prevent co-processing of adhering contaminations.

substeps.instruction: Expose the periosteum and medullary cavity surfaces to UV light for 15min each.

steps.title: Grind Bone to Powder
steps.instruction: Grind the sample to a fine powder using a mixer mill (MM2000, Retsch) or an agate mortar and pestle, depending on material consistency.

steps.title: Decalcify Bone Powder
steps.instruction: Mix 0.3g bone powder with 1.5ml EDTA-solution (0.5M, pH 8.3) in a 2ml reaction tube.

substeps.instruction: Vortex the mixture vigorously (e.g., Vortex Genie 2, VWRbrand).
Incubate for 48h at 20˚C with constant rotation or agitation (using an incubator or shaking water bath).

steps.title: Separate Supernatant
steps.instruction: Pellet the remaining bone powder by centrifugation for 5min at 6000rpm (desktop centrifuge 5415C, Eppendorf).

substeps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant (ca. 1300µl) to a 5ml polypropylene round-bottom tube (Falcon).

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with Silica
steps.instruction: Transfer the aqueous supernatant to a 14ml polypropylene round-bottom tube (Falcon).

substeps.instruction: Evaluate the pH of the solution (e.g., PH-Indicator Strips, pH 6.5-10, Merck).
If necessary, adjust the pH to 7.5 by adding further sodium acetate buffer (2M, pH 4.5).
Add 3250µl Isopropanol (abs., RT), 60-120µl sodium acetate buffer (2M, pH 4.5), and 5µl silica solution (Glasmilk™ Bio 101).

steps.title: Recover DNA-Silica Pellet
steps.instruction: Separate the precipitate by centrifugation for 2min at 4000rpm (Centrifuge 5804, Eppendorf).

substeps.instruction: Discard the supernatant by careful decanting.

steps.title: Wash and Dry Pellet
steps.instruction: Wash the DNA-silica pellet with 500µl EtOH (abs.).

substeps.instruction: Remove the alcohol by centrifugation for 2min at 4000rpm (Centrifuge 5804, Eppendorf).
Allow the pellet to air dry for ca. 30min at RT.

steps.title: Optional Extract Cleaning
steps.instruction: If the extract is brownish or PCR inhibition occurs (indicating humic acids), perform additional cleaning.

substeps.instruction: Use ultrafiltration dialysis or the Wizard PCR Prep™ DNA Purification System (Promega) following a modified protocol.
